Recently, more and more users have reported that their Mac experiences a rainbow spinning wheel when running macOS 26.5, with some saying their trackpad becomes completely unresponsive for several seconds at a time.

Activity Monitor typically shows three 'culprits', and there now appears to be a reliable fix for this issue…

I mentioned this issue last month and speculated it might be related to Apple Intelligence's photo scanning feature. When checking Activity Monitor, you typically find that one, two, or three processes are using a high amount of CPU.

Macworld's Michael Simon has also been troubled by this issue.

He tried various methods without success, and eventually found one that worked: deleting the ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight folder. This of course means the Mac needs to rebuild the Spotlight index, but he said the issue did not recur after two weeks. My own experience has been less than a day, but so far I have not seen the problem return either.

If you're willing to wait for Spotlight data to be rebuilt, here's how to delete the data:

  • Open a Finder window
  • From the 'Go' menu, select 'Go to Folder…'
  • Paste: ~/Library/Metadata/CoreSpotlight
  • Press CMD-A to select all, then right-click on any item and choose 'Move to Trash'
  • Right-click on the Trash and select 'Empty Trash'
  • Confirm when prompted

If you're also experiencing this issue, please let us know in the comments whether this method works for you too.
